summary: A bordered surface that groups one part of a page, with an optional title row. A titled card is a named region; an untitled one is a plain surface.
useWhen: a page is several distinct groups — settings sections, dashboard panels, a log beside a chart
a group needs a title, a one-line description or a single action like "All runs"
a loading placeholder needs the same frame as the content it stands in for

useInstead.when: it is a feature row with a headline, text and a media panel
it is one headline figure and how it moved
the content is a list of settings, each with a label and a control
the message needs the user's attention now rather than a place on the page

composition.note: The title row is built from props — `title`, `description`, `action` — so every card lays it out the same way. The body is `children`, spaced 12 apart by the card's grid.
composition.example: All runs}>…

default.use: every card that is not a danger zone

danger.use: a card of irreversible actions — delete the workspace, transfer ownership. The rule turns red; the title must still say what is at stake

guarantees: a titled card renders a <section> named by its heading, so it is a landmark a screen reader can jump to
an untitled card renders a <div>, never an unnamed <section>
the danger intent is a border colour only, so the meaning stays in the words
requires: the right `headingLevel` for where the card sits in the page outline
`isRegion={false}` when the card's only content is a landmark named by the same words, such as a Table labelled by the card's title
notes: `headingLevel` takes 2-6 and defaults to 2. It is a number rather than a variant because it is an outline decision, not a visual one: the title looks the same at every level.
`description` renders only under a `title`. An untitled card has no title row to put it in.

antiPatterns.dont: a heading passed in `children` instead of `title`
antiPatterns.why: the card does not become a named region, and the title row loses its layout for `description` and `action`
the title row wraps and the card reads as a toolbar; `action` is for one control — put the rest in the body
a red border is not read aloud and is easy to miss; the title and the button labels must say what cannot be undone
border inside border reads as a mistake; group the inner content with a heading or a Divider instead
